tasks.title: The store census refuses an INFLATED store and has no equivalent for a DEFLATED one — deletion is an unguarded route to a green PASS
tasks.description: RAISED BY T156 as follow-up F-3 and RE-DERIVED BY THE DRIVER before being written as a task (P-42). CONFIRMED at nexus/internal/apps/loanschedule/conformance/vector.go: DuplicateCaseIDs refuses an INFLATED store (two files declaring one case_id) and its own comment states the ground -- coverage numbers are sums over loaded vectors, and LoadStore takes the census over every context directory BEFORE applying -context, closing T119's F-T119-1. There is NO equivalent in the DEFLATED direction. THE ASYMMETRY IS STRUCTURAL, NOT AN OVERSIGHT IN ONE FUNCTION: a vector that has been REMOVED is absent from BOTH enumerators, so `find` and LoadStore AGREE, any census that compares the two is satisfied, and the store grades green one vector short. T154's LEG 3 census refuses any .json the harness did not load -- that is inflation by construction and CANNOT catch deflation. MEASURED CONSEQUENCE (T156, reproduced on a scratch store): delete exactly one parity vector file and the harness prints 'VERDICT: PASS (exit 0) -- 42 parity vectors ... 5576 cells compared', exit 0, NO WARNING ANYWHERE, against the driver's own verified 43/5664 on main this fire. T156 fixed ONE CAUSE of deflation (an unguarded mv in one rig). ANY OTHER CAUSE GIVES THE SAME SILENT GREEN -- a failed checkout, a bad merge, a .gitignore, a stray rm, a worktree prune. THE ONLY THING THAT CAN DISTINGUISH 'this store is COMPLETE' from 'this store is SELF-CONSISTENT' is a COMMITTED MANIFEST OF EXPECTED case_ids that the harness refuses to run without. tasks.title: The wrapper DETECTS the exit-protocol violation and does NOTHING about it — a WARN with no consequence let four killed workers stay `in_progress` across two fires
tasks.description:
MEASURED BY THE DRIVER, local fire 20260823-080004, from the logs of the two preceding fires. This is a P-45 instance in the WRAPPER itself: a guard that fires, prints, and changes nothing.

WHAT HAPPENED, in order, all of it in `~/Library/Logs/gerege-nbfi/`:
  1. Fire `20260822-140002` ran from 14:00 to **22:52** (its log is 1,061,986 bytes), dispatched T271/T283/T285/T286, and then ENDED ITS TURN. STEP 5.5: 'NEVER exit with live workers -- they die with you.' All four died. It left them `in_progress` in tasks.json and did NOT rewrite RESUME.md.
  2. That run exhausted the FIVE-HOUR quota window.
  3. Fire `20260822-230001` started 8 minutes later and got **HTTP 429, rateLimitType=five_hour, resetsAt=1787414400 (midnight Asia/Ulaanbaatar)** -- `RESULT success :: You've hit your session limit`. **It never got a single turn.** rc=1 at 23:00:21, 20 seconds after start. A whole ORACLE-REACHING window spent on nothing, and the stale `in_progress` claim went uncorrected a second time.
  4. At 23:00:32 the wrapper printed:
         WARN: exit-protocol violation -- .softhouse/RESUME.md predates this fire's start;
               the next fire may act on stale state. Review it by hand.
     **IT WAS RIGHT, AND IT DID NOTHING.** 'Review it by hand' is prose, and PROSE DOES NOT FIRE ON THE NEXT FIRE (P-89/P-45). Nobody reviewed it by hand, because the only thing that reads that log is the next fire, which reads RESUME.md instead.

THE DEFECT IS NOT THE 14:00 FIRE'S BEHAVIOUR -- that is a driver error already recorded. **The defect is that the wrapper is the ONLY component that survives a driver's death, detects the violation correctly, and then declines to act.** The 08:00 fire had to reconstruct all of this by hand from six `rescued-agent-*` branch names and two log files.

WHAT TO BUILD (measure before you build -- P-82: build the suggestion, MEASURE it, and report the zero if it is zero):
  A. **At fire EXIT, reconcile tasks.json against reality.** For every task `in_progress`, check whether a live worker process/worktree actually corresponds to it. If not, rewrite it to `needs_retry` with a note naming the fire that killed it and the `softhouse/rescued-agent-*-<fireid>` branch its WIP landed on -- the sweep ALREADY computes that mapping when it decides to KEEP a worktree, and then throws it away. Commit and push the correction. STEP 5.4 already REQUIRES this of the driver; the point is that a dead driver cannot do it, so the wrapper must.
  B. **Escalate the RESUME.md staleness WARN from prose to a recorded fact** the next fire cannot miss -- write it into the repo (a committed marker), not only into a log nobody reads.

tasks.title: THE WRAPPER EDITS ITSELF WHILE RUNNING: merging T288 grew fire-program.sh from 45,665 to 64,888 bytes mid-execution, and zsh reads a script incrementally by byte offset
tasks.description:
RAISED BY THE DRIVER IN FIRE 20260824-000016, at the moment of merging T288, and recorded rather than waved through.

`.softhouse/bin/fire-program.sh` is the zsh script that RUNS each local fire. It launches `claude` as a foreground child that works for HOURS, and it has a long tail afterwards -- lock release, worktree prune, and now T288's in_progress reconciliation. It has NO SELF-SNAPSHOT: the interpreter is reading the same file on disk that the fire it started is free to modify.

Merging T288 grew that file from 45,665 to 64,888 bytes WHILE IT WAS BEING READ -- a 19 KB insertion above the running interpreter's unread tail. zsh, like bash, reads a script incrementally and seeks by BYTE OFFSET; it does not re-parse from the top. So the running wrapper's remaining commands can be resumed at a shifted offset and misparsed. The driver verified `zsh -n` clean after the merge and pushed anyway, on the reasoning that losing the work was worse and that the blast radius is bounded (the LOCK names a pid on THIS host, so the next fire treats a dead holder as free immediately, regardless of age). THAT IS A MITIGATION, NOT A FIX, AND IT WAS AN UNREVIEWED JUDGEMENT CALL -- treat it as such.

THE FIX TO EVALUATE: have the wrapper re-exec itself from an immutable snapshot -- copy itself (and lib-worktree-prune.zsh, which it sources) to a temp path on start, `exec` the copy with a guard variable so it does not loop, and let the repo copy be freely modified by the fire it started. Cheap, standard, and it makes wrapper changes mergeable by the very fire they improve. CONSIDER AND RECORD what it costs: `${0:A:h}` currently resolves SCRIPT_DIR against the script's own path and is used to source the prune library -- a snapshot changes what that resolves to, and getting it wrong replaces a rare corruption with a certain breakage. Also decide what happens if the snapshot copy fails.

EVALUATE THE ALTERNATIVE HONESTLY TOO: forbid merging bin/ changes from inside a fire, and hand them to the cloud fire or a human. That is a convention someone must remember, and P-45 says a guard that only works when someone remembers to run it enforces nothing -- so it is probably the wrong answer, but say why rather than assuming.

DRIVE IT, because this is exactly the class of bug that reasoning gets wrong: construct a long zsh script that sleeps, modify it mid-run by inserting bytes above the unread region, and OBSERVE what the interpreter does. Do that for the CURRENT wrapper shape and for the snapshot shape, and commit both transcripts. If the hazard turns out NOT to reproduce on this zsh, that is a publishable negative result -- say so plainly and record the version, rather than shipping a fix for a bug that does not exist.

SCOPE: fire-program.sh and your own rig. DO NOT modify .softhouse/LOCK, tasks.json or RESUME.md -- a live fire may be using all three. Verify with `bash .softhouse/conformance.sh` and `.softhouse/bin/fire-program.sh --probe`. P-84: exit 2 with NO probe line printed is not an oracle outage. Handoff to .softhouse/handoff/2026-08-21-run2-tierA-gl-accounting-A2/T301.md. P-86: cite the rule TEXT beside any P-number.

BUT THE IMMUNITY IS LAYOUT, NOT DESIGN, and the task proved it: appending 15KB of top-level code after the chain loop (an ordinary future edit) brings the hazard back -- FRAGILE reached YES / FRAGILE-SNAP no / CONTROL reached YES. Sharper mechanism than the brief stated: a SPLICE AT THE READ BOUNDARY needing no shift at all. TWO CORRECTIONS TO T309's COMMENT, WHICH THE DRIVER HAD RELAYED AS SETTLED FACT AND RE-MEASURED BY INODE AT MERGE: `sed -i ''` writes a NEW inode so it is ISOLATED (T309 and the driver's briefs wrongly called it dangerous), and `cp` writes the SAME inode so it IS dangerous (omitted by both). tasks.title: THE CORPSE SWEEP IS A HAND-TYPED GLOB AND IT RETURNED A FALSE 'ALL EMPTY' — make it an instrument, and make case-shadowing impossible to create

tasks.title: FU-T279-3 REFRAMED by T280's F-C: the post-checkout hook CANNOT REFUSE on this git — decide what, if anything, is worth installing
tasks.description:
*** THIS TASK'S ORIGINAL PREMISE WAS REFUTED BEFORE IT RAN, AND THE REFUTATION IS THE STARTING POINT. ***

The driver filed this one hour ago as 'INSTALL the post-checkout push-before-spawn hook', gated on T280's review precisely because a hook that refuses worktree creation could brick every future fire. **T280 came back and said the hook cannot refuse at all.**

THE REAL QUESTION, NOW THAT REFUSAL IS OFF THE TABLE. The obligation to enforce is: *the LOCK, the dispatch record and the in-flight RESUME.md are pushed BEFORE the first `git worktree add` of a batch.* It has been missed twice by drivers who had read the rule (101 s late on 2026-08-22; 135 s late, two of three artefacts, earlier in THIS fire) — and OBEYED once, this iteration, with a +40 s minimum margin (`.softhouse/observations/20260828-push-before-spawn-OBEYED-and-measured.md`). If some other hook (`reference-transaction`, `pre-receive` on a local remote) CAN veto, measure it rather than assume it.

Wiring it into the exit protocol turns a silent convention into a recorded violation. Weakest deterrent, cheapest, and it CANNOT brick a fire — say whether that trade is right.
  (d) **Nothing is worth it.** A legitimate answer if you can show it. Say so plainly and record why, rather than installing something that will be cited later as enforcement it is not.

tasks.title: F-A: lock_released_at() declares a LIVE lock FREE when `released_at` is the last key — a one-line fail-open in the arm that has already caused a double-holder incident
tasks.description:
*** THIS IS A FAIL-OPEN IN THE LOCK PROTOCOL. Its failure mode is TWO ORCHESTRATORS HOLDING THE REPO AT ONCE, which is P-85, which on 2026-08-22 killed four worker branches with its sandbox. Treat it accordingly: narrow, measured, and driven RED before and GREEN after. ***

RAISED BY T280 (merged 346b7a1d) as F-A, BLOCKING. THE DRIVER RE-DERIVED IT FROM THE SHIPPED SOURCE before filing this task rather than trusting the review [VERIFIED: read .softhouse/bin/fire-program.sh:120-131 at commit 346b7a1d].

THE DEFECT, exactly. `lock_released_at()` does:
    v="${${body#*\"released_at\":}%%,*}"
    v="${v//[$' \t\r\n\"']/}"
    [[ "$v" == null || -z "$v" ]] && return 0
The first line cuts at the first COMMA. The strip class removes space, tab, CR, LF and double-quote — and NOT the closing brace. So a LOCK whose `"released_at": null` is the LAST KEY has no following comma, the cut takes everything to end of file, and the strip leaves the NON-EMPTY string `null}`. `null}` != `null`, so the function returns a value, ARM 1 FIRES, and a lock held by a live process owned by this very user is declared FREE-released.

T280 measured it end to end with `pid_state=alive_here`, and reproduced it from a hand-written body AND from both `json.dumps` forms. Its probe is at `.softhouse/reviews/t280-review-t279/probe/drive-releasedat-failopen.zsh` with output under `out/`. **RE-RUN THAT PROBE FIRST AND SEE IT FAIL** (P-22) — you have not seen the defect until you have seen it.

REACHABILITY, STATED HONESTLY BY THE REVIEWER AND NOT HIDDEN BY THE DRIVER: nothing in this repo ever WRITES `released_at` — the wrapper releases the lock by `rm -f`. So arm 1's only possible input is a HAND-WRITTEN LOCK. That is not a reason to downgrade it: STEP 0 exists precisely to govern the hand-run case, arm 1 is written for it, and **the most natural way to hand-write that file — `released_at` last, as `json.dumps` of a dict built in the obvious order — triggers it.** Say in your handoff whether you agree with that reachability argument; if you think it is overstated, argue it, because an overstated severity is also a defect.

THE FIX T280 MEASURED, and the trap next to it. `v="${v%%\}*}"` works. **The obvious variant — adding `{}` to the strip class — DOES NOT COMPILE UNDER zsh**, and T280 says so; find out why before you reach for it, because a fix that does not parse is a fix that silently is not there. `.softhouse/reviews/t280-review-t279/probe/fixcheck.zsh` exists — run it.

DO NOT STOP AT THE ONE LINE. The real question is whether `lock_released_at()` is the ONLY reader with this shape. `lock_started_age()` sits immediately below it and parses the same body the same way. **Audit every field reader in `fire-program.sh` that pulls a value out of the LOCK JSON by string surgery**, and for each one state what it does when its key is last, when the value is a string containing a comma, when the key appears twice, and when the body is not valid JSON at all. tasks.title: EVALUATE (do not install) the PreToolUse deny hook — the only remaining mechanism that could actually refuse a spawn
tasks.description:
RAISED BY T336 as the one untested candidate, and it is filed with a deliberate restriction: **your deliverable is a measurement and a recommendation, NOT an installation.**

WHY IT IS THE LAST CANDIDATE. T336 established that no git hook can work on the spawn route — the harness creates worker worktrees **without running git hooks at all** [measured with a control; see its handoff]. It separately found that `reference-transaction` in `prepared` genuinely CAN abort `git worktree add` (rc 255, no branch, no directory) — a true precondition, and useless here for the same reason. That exhausts git. A `PreToolUse` deny hook, configured in `.claude/settings.json`, is the only mechanism left that could refuse a spawn before it happens. **T336 did not test it**, correctly: it is a harness-configuration change and a worker may not make one.

**WHY YOU MAY NOT INSTALL IT EITHER, and this is the driver's ruling, not timidity.** A `PreToolUse` deny hook that misfires does not fail like a bad guard — it **refuses tool calls for every future session in this repo**, including the sessions that would be needed to remove it. That is the precise risk the driver gated T336 on ('a hook that refuses worktree creation can brick every future fire'), and T336's own evidence has now shown the driver was right to gate it, since the hook it was sent to install would never have fired at all. So: **build it, drive it RED and GREEN in a SCRATCH settings file in a throwaway directory, measure it, and report.** Do not write to the repo's `.claude/settings.json`.

WHAT THE MEASUREMENT MUST ANSWER, and any one of these coming back badly is a reason to recommend AGAINST:
  1. Does a `PreToolUse` deny actually prevent the Agent tool's worktree spawn, or only a direct `Bash` `git worktree add`? These are different call paths and only one of them is how workers are created.
  2. What does the hook have access to at decision time? It must determine whether the dispatch record is PUSHED — which means reading `origin/main`, which means a network call inside a hook that runs on every tool use. Cost it.
  3. **The failure mode when it cannot decide.** Offline, or `origin` unreachable: refusing every spawn bricks the fire; allowing every spawn is the guard not existing. Both answers are bad; say which is less bad and why.
  4. The escape hatch, and proof it cannot become the default path. An escape hatch everyone uses is the guard not existing (T336 rejected candidate (a) on exactly this ground for the warn variant).
  5. **Recovery.** If the hook denies wrongly, what removes it? If the answer requires a session that the hook itself blocks, the design is disqualified regardless of how well it works when correct.

A recommendation of **'do not install'** is a fully acceptable outcome and T336 already reached that shape for three of its four candidates. What is NOT acceptable is a recommendation to install based on a mechanism you have not seen refuse a real spawn.
